brand_note: Ronav R1 confirmed on the Ronav data sheet (ronav.ae, a UAE marine positioning brand). No clean product photo of the R1 receiver or display was found; the only official image is the RX45 GNSS antenna that ships in the R1 system.
official_name: Ronav R1 GNSS/DGPS receiver system (R1 receiver, RX45 antenna, Rovision display)
description: The Ronav R1 is a quad-band GNSS receiver using GPS, GLONASS and BeiDou, with Galileo and QZSS ready, aimed at marine oil and gas positioning. It supports L-band corrections, SBAS and external RTCM or RTK inputs, and is paired with the RX45 antenna and an optional 12 inch Rovision touch display with Ronav Monitor software.
features: L-band DGPS corrections down to 2 cm RMS quoted by Ronav
RTK baseline up to 50 km, accepts ROX, RTCM, CMR and CMR+

images.shows: RX45 GNSS antenna cut-out (the antenna of the R1 system, not the receiver)

notes: Receiver and display images exist only inside the datasheet PDF (not extractable as URLs here). Request a photo from Ronav if the receiver itself must be shown.

brand_note: Confirmed. The 9410-AUT is Fugro's combined position and correction receiver; the support site notes it shares a hardware platform with the Trimble MPS566.
description: The Fugro Seastar 9410-AUT is Fugro's current combined GNSS position and correction receiver, successor to the 9205-GNSS, with enhancements for Dynamic Positioning use. It works with all GNSS constellations and supports Fugro's G4 augmentation and SatGuard NMA (Navigation Message Authentication) service.
features: Combined receiver and demodulator for Fugro correction services
Supports G4 and SatGuard NMA service
Same hardware platform as Trimble MPS566
notes: Numeric specs not on the pages read. A search snippet of the brochure (scribd copy, not read in full) mentions 10 cm accuracy; not used as a spec. Kit contents (antenna etc.) not verified.

brand_note: Confirmed on veripos.com; Veripos is part of Hexagon.
description: The LD900 is a quad-band, multi-constellation GNSS receiver for critical marine work such as DP, offshore construction and survey. It has an independent L-band input for a dedicated correction antenna and keeps working through multipath and scintillation. It has a colour display and a 72-hour rolling data log.
features: Multi-channel L-band for Apex and Ultra PPP services
EN60945 certified, OGP 373-19 and IMCA SO15 QC compliant
Optional ALIGN heading and MSK beacon
Compatible with SPAN GNSS+INS and GRIT

images.shows: LD900 straight front view (press release image)

notes: Register says 'LD900 (set)'; set contents not verified.

official_name: Clear-Com Encore analog partyline system (main station and speaker stations)
description: Encore is Clear-Com's analog partyline intercom family. A two- or four-channel main station supplies intercom and power to connected beltpacks, wall stations and remote or speaker stations over standard two-conductor shielded cable. Systems are full-duplex and can be expanded or tied to other partyline systems.
features: MS-702 2-channel 1RU and MS-704 4-channel 2RU main stations, both with built-in speaker
Runs on standard two-conductor shielded mic cable
Speaker stations for wall or desktop-enclosure mounting (KB-702 2-channel)
Expandable, with IP link to further beltpacks via LQ interfaces

Up to 4 radar sensors interconnected over Ethernet
Dedicated keyboard with trackball and rotary knobs

brand_note: CONFIRMED: Inertial Labs (inertiallabs.com) makes MRU-B1, MRU-B1.1, MRU-B2 (plus E, P, PD and subsea versions); MRU-B2 is also sold as a rental unit by Norwegian Offshore Rental and by Ocean Science Technology. Caution: Inertial Labs' table lists B1 as heave/surge/sway only and B1.1 as pitch and roll, whereas the register says 'B1 (roll and pitch)'. The register B1 may actually be the MRU-B1.1; Kongsberg also makes unrelated 'MRU' units. Verify the exact model on delivered units.
official_name: Inertial Labs MRU-B2 Motion Reference Unit (family: MRU-B1, B1.1, B2)
description: Inertial Labs' MRU-B2 is a compact strap-down MEMS motion sensor that outputs heave, surge, sway, pitch and roll. It can emit Kongsberg Seatex and Teledyne TSS data formats so it can replace older MRUs, and the range carries an ABS design assessment certificate. Subsea (1000 m) versions are listed for the B-series.
features: MRU-B2: heave, surge, sway, pitch and roll
MRU-B1: heave, surge, sway; MRU-B1.1: pitch and roll (per Inertial Labs table)
Seatex and TSS-1 compatible output formats
notes: Image pixel sizes not reported in tool output (set to 0). The B1 / B1.1 output mapping comes from a markdown-flattened table; re-check against the datasheet (inertiallabs.com/mru-datasheet) before printing.

brand_note: Confirmed: R.M. Young (YOUNG) Model 86106 Ultrasonic Anemometer - Marine. 'With wind display' is not part of the sensor; no display read.
description: The YOUNG 86106 is a compact 2-axis ultrasonic anemometer with no moving parts, measuring horizontal wind speed and direction. The marine version is preconfigured for NMEA serial output (RS-485, 4800 baud), with analog and 4-20 mA outputs also available. It mounts on a standard 1 inch pipe.
features: Preconfigured NMEA output; RS-232, RS-485 and several formats available
Mounts on 1 inch IPS pipe with orientation ring

brand_note: Confirmed. OMC-118 is Observator's stainless-steel ultrasonic wind sensor; Observator's manual and marinsat/nauticexpo datasheets describe it as based on the Gill WindObserver II (search excerpts only). OMC-122M bracket not researched.

It outputs NMEA or polar format and connects to Observator loggers, signal conditioning units and displays. The standard range is 0 to 65 m/s with 0 to 75 m/s optional.
features: Analogue and NMEA outputs, user-selectable format
Connects to the Observator display line
notes: Datasheet PDF link on the page (Datasheet-OMC-118-V20210805.pdf) not opened.

Automatic speed and latitude error correction
